failure_modes.evidence: Summary_1 states: 'The passages do not identify who wrote this work. To verify the claim, a retrieval system must find: - The full identity of the author of the novel "Love and Mr Lewisham" - Whether this author is award-winning and what awards they have received - The author's nationality.' However, this summary does NOT name the specific missing entity 'H. G. Wells' or specify needing information about 'H. G. Wells nationality' or 'H. G. Wells awards.' It only describes the type of information needed (author identity, awards, nationality) without naming the actual missing entity that retrieval should target.

failure_modes.name: Verdict_Despite_Insufficiency
failure_modes.evidence: Summary_2 states: 'The claim is VERIFIED AS TRUE. H. G. Wells, the author of "Love and Mr Lewisham" (1900), was English, while Rubén Darío was Nicaraguan.' However, the passages provided in hop 2 do NOT contain H. G. Wells's nationality - passage [3] only states he authored the novel but does not specify he was English. The solver renders a definitive verdict claiming Wells 'was English' without this fact being established in the retrieved evidence, relying instead on external knowledge ('this is well-established historical fact, though not explicitly stated in these passages').

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 2 solver reasoning, the solver processes multiple irrelevant passages: 'Mr. Sammler's Planet' (Saul Bellow), 'What Was Lost' (Catherine O'Flynn), 'Mr. Darcy's Daughters' (Elizabeth Aston), 'Valentine' (George Sand), 'Ten Novels and Their Authors' (Somerset Maugham), and 'Dora Dueck' biography. None of these passages relate to the claim about 'Love and Mr Lewisham' or Rubén Darío, yet the solver includes them all in the passages section without explicitly filtering or dismissing their irrelevance, diverting from focused verification.
